sources.entry: mail-archiver - Web application for archiving, searching, and exporting emails from multiple accounts (IMAP, M365 or Import). Featuring folder sync, attachment support, mailbox migration and a dashboard. GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Mail-Archiver is a self-hostable web application that archives, searches, and exports email from multiple IMAP, Microsoft 365, and import-only accounts, run via Docker with PostgreSQL.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs scheduled syncs that archive mail from multiple accounts into a PostgreSQL-backed store, with a web UI for browsing and searching them. Search supports filters, and emails can be previewed with attachments. Accounts or selected emails can be exported as mbox or zipped EML. It supports IMAP accounts, Microsoft 365 mailboxes via Microsoft Graph, Microsoft personal accounts via OAuth2 device code flow, and import-only accounts, plus MBox and EML (ZIP) import with folder structure. It also offers a read-only REST API with per-user API keys, an optional MCP endpoint for AI agents, multi-user permissions, a dashboard, retention policies, a deletion lock, and an access log.
use_cases: export mail as mbox or EML
apply retention rules to mail on the server
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml with the mailarchive-app service (image s1t5/mailarchiver:latest) and a postgres:17-alpine service
Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD and the matching ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection password to a secure value
Set Authentication__Username and Authentication__Password for the admin user
Put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front of the app on port 5000
Run docker compose up -d, then docker compose restart
notable: Read-only REST API and optional MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint for AI agents, using scoped per-user API keys
Microsoft 365 tenant bulk import from a single form, plus Microsoft personal account support without an Azure app registration
Mailbox migration that copies emails between mailboxes while keeping folder structure
Deletion lock via DeletionPolicy__DeletionAllowed=false for compliance use
UI available in 14 languages with dark mode
caveats: The app does not provide HTTPS itself; a reverse proxy is required
Documentation is described as still fresh and being expanded
Code changes from third parties require prior coordination with the maintainer by email
